purpose: Specify the atomic durable claim/pin mechanism required for many identical generic workers to select distinct READY opportunities without duplicate substantive execution.
authority_boundary: A successful claim grants only the predeclared execution scope of one opportunity. It is not Current/Human Accepted/Served authority and cannot widen owner, privacy or write boundaries.
selection_flow: load Continuity Head plus queue projection
filter READY opportunities by capability/tool/privacy/write-scope compatibility
rank eligible candidates by durable project priority, dependency readiness, information/unblock value and collision risk
if the claim loses a race, do not overwrite; reload evidence and try another eligible opportunity
after claim success, create/persist execution attempt and STARTED before substantive work
atomicity_rule: Exclusive claim creation must be atomic create-if-absent, compare-and-swap, database uniqueness/transaction or another host primitive with collision evidence. A read-then-unconditional-write sequence is forbidden.
lifecycle_rules: Claim exists but STARTED absent means CLAIMED_NOT_STARTED.
STARTED is persisted before material execution.
RETURNED requires a durable return artifact.
DONE requires durable return unless the exact opportunity contract explicitly allows a no-return terminal.
A worker chat disappearing leaves durable attempt state for recovery instead of forcing human archaeology.

stale_and_retry.stale_definition: STALE is derived only from an explicit freshness/lease/heartbeat policy plus durable timestamps/evidence; elapsed conversational silence alone is insufficient.
stale_and_retry.reclaim_rule: A stale claim is never overwritten in place. A new claim/attempt references the stale predecessor and proves the policy that authorized reclamation.
stale_and_retry.retry_rule: Retry gets a new run/attempt identity and preserves all previous claims, STARTED, RETURN, failure and side-effect evidence.
stale_and_retry.side_effect_rule: Potentially effectful retries require idempotency keys/receipts or verified compensating/rollback boundaries before repetition.

collision_rules: Two live workers may inspect the same READY candidate, but only one may obtain its exclusive claim.
Losing a race is normal control flow, not failure and never authorizes overwrite.
Independent read-only critic/research opportunities may use a non-exclusive claim mode only when that mode is explicit in the opportunity contract.
Write-scope collisions remain independently checked even after opportunity-level claim success.
post_return_rule: After durable RETURN/DONE, a worker may run the bounded POST_RETURN scan defined by the operating model. It must acquire a fresh valid claim for any new substantive opportunity; retaining chat context is not continuing authority.
required_falsification_tests: 2-worker exclusive race: exactly one claim succeeds
5-worker race: no opportunity receives duplicate exclusive substantive execution
losing worker reloads and claims a different READY opportunity when available
claim exists but worker vanishes before STARTED and parent can distinguish the state
worker vanishes after STARTED and stale policy eventually exposes recoverable state without inventing DONE
stale reclamation produces a new attempt linked to predecessor rather than overwrite
RETURN exists but DONE is missing and projection preserves that mismatch
retry of effectful work is blocked without required idempotency/side-effect evidence
privacy/authority incompatibility blocks claim regardless of priority
post-return second job requires a new claim and cannot inherit write authority from the prior job
promotion_gate: full B-BIGPIC convergence including WI-BIG-09 and WI-BIG-13
host primitive for atomic claim selected and tested
generic /w remains non-operational until those canaries pass
